research_updates.title: Campus identity and chronology resolved
research_updates.notes: Source families checked: IM3 inventory, Google location and sustainability pages, Douglas County assessor records, Georgia EPD permits, and contemporaneous expansion reporting. The project boundary is the Google-operated campus at 300 Riverside Parkway on authority-owned parcel 08741820001. Google dates its Douglas County presence to 2003 and first data-center opening to 2007; the assessor dates Computer Data Centers improvements to 2006 and 2016 and a utility building to 2011. Later Google Georgia projects in LaGrange and Columbia County, an account at 2201 Thornton Road, unrelated Douglas County DRI data-center proposals, and off-site solar projects are not collapsed into the campus.

research_updates.title: Assessor and taxpayer-account audit separates taxable and exempt stocks
research_updates.notes: Repositories and routes checked: Douglas qPublic real- and personal-property searches, linked-account tables, Board of Tax Assessors agendas, 2019-2024 County ACFR principal-taxpayer and millage exhibits, Georgia DOR property-record and millage files, and exact Google/DADC/address/parcel/account queries. P88150 is the directly named Google account; P79020 is authority-owned with Google tax-department linkage and fully exempt assessed value. The 2026 account and parcel stocks are recorded separately. The March 5, 2025 BTA agenda's P79020 amended-return figures conflict with the retained live historical 2024 figure and are documented as interim or superseded, not recorded. P97430 at 2201 Thornton Road and contractor, food-service, Waymo, logistics, or empty linked accounts are excluded. County totals, real parcel value, and account components overlap and are not summed.

source.title: Douglas County personal-property account P79020
source.notes: The account search identifies the Development Authority of Douglas County, with Google Inc. Tax Department mailing information, at 300 Riverside Parkway and links the account to real parcel 08741820001. research_updates.title: Tax-bill and payment audit resolves both personal-property accounts
research_updates.notes: Repositories and routes checked: Tax Commissioner pages and reports, Georgia DOR payment routing and 2023-2025 millage files, GovernmentWindow map-code and bill-detail workflows, qPublic histories, County ACFR tax collections/millage exhibits, document-center search, and exact queries for P79020, P88150, 08741820001, Google, DADC, and 300 Riverside Parkway. Cloudflare verification cleared automatically during the independent orchestration audit. P79020 bill 1075743 supplies eleven 2015-2025 zero ordinary-tax bills plus annual fair-market values for the fully exempt authority account. P88150 bill 1077031 supplies eleven exact ordinary-tax bills and paid totals with payment dates. The 2025 P88150 bill reconciles the qPublic $15,560,354 assessed value to $38,900,884 statement fair-market value (entity table rounds to $38,900,885), a 31.413-mill net rate after county sales-tax credit, and $488,797.40 total tax. These account observations do not establish PILOT or lease payments, recipient distributions, same-scope public costs, net fiscal benefit, or a selected-building allocation. Historical DDCWSA utility-service revenue remains separate from property tax.

research_updates.title: Water, sewer, electricity, and environmental search resolves location water only
research_updates.notes: Repositories and routes checked: Google 2023-2025 environmental/impact disclosures; DDCWSA 2014, 2016, and 2025 financial reports, work-session agendas, rates, and capital/bond materials; Georgia EPD NPDES notices, air records, orders, complaints, and DMR routing; EPA ECHO facility report for GA0038920/FRS 110061650100; Georgia Power/PSC tariffs and Docket 55378; and operator energy disclosures. The 2016 WSA comparative table supports four direct service/year observations: 2007 water and sewer, plus 2016 sewer and stormwater customer revenue. They use the utility-service-payment metric, never the infrastructure-fund metric, and remain incomplete annual coverage; 2016 water top-ten absence is not zero. ECHO displays 0.18 MGD average facility flow in 2026, annualized with a rounding band in modeled synthesis. Utility revenue, Google water consumption, off-site 78.8 MW contracted solar, PUE, DMR flow, generic rates, bills, and public infrastructure are kept distinct. No meter, complete/current Google bill, tier/ERU inputs, peak-day demand, campus kWh/load, interconnection cost, selected-building allocation, or Google-specific capital obligation was found.

research_updates.title: Workforce, payroll, training, and procurement audit preserves only reported headcount
research_updates.notes: Repositories and routes checked: the 2015 expansion announcement; 2016 DDCWSA principal-employer table; current and archived Google Careers queries; Georgia/Douglas workforce-development, grant, training, and development-agreement pages; recipient sources and Form 990 search; permit contractors; BLS QCEW 2015 annual file; and exact employee/payroll/wage/residence/apprenticeship/transfer/procurement terms. The operator's more-than-350 June 2015 campus snapshot, local table's 300 in 2016, and 25-job projection are retained with different dates and definitions; the discrepancy prevents interpolation. A 350-employee threshold wage-bill sensitivity uses Douglas County's $684 all-industry 2015 annual-average weekly wage, explicitly not observed Google payroll. No annual-average FTE, Google wage distribution, benefits, contractor headcount, worker residence, training completions, transfer ledger, or local hiring outcome was found.

research_updates.title: County outcome and public-cost candidates fail causal and fiscal prerequisites
research_updates.notes: BLS QCEW, BEA county accounts, Census business and population context, County ACFRs and budgets, and development records were checked for employment, establishments, wages, income, GDP, population, property-tax share, capital spending, public safety, roads, water, and debt from 2001 through the latest complete vintages. Google dates local presence to 2003 and opening to 2007, while concurrent county growth, multiple later data centers, boundary changes, the 2008 recession, and missing treatment-share and comparison diagnostics prevent a defensible project effect. County totals remain context only. No same-scope marginal service cost, attributable infrastructure outlay, fiscal recipient distribution, or validated counterfactual was found.

research_updates.title: Fourth-pass model audit retains bounded anchor-based estimates and rejects unsupported chains
research_updates.notes: Candidate-by-candidate disposition after directed exhaustion: retain three unallocated 2022-2024 water-consumption conversions; annualize the displayed 2026 ECHO DMR average flow with a rounding band; calculate two county-M&O-only gross-levy counterfactuals from exempt P79020 assessed value and published millage; apply Douglas County's 2015 all-industry QCEW wage to the operator's 350-employee threshold with a 75%-125% wage sensitivity; and apply a national 2022 construction payroll/receipts ratio to the sole valued 2025 remodel with 0.5-1.5 transfer sensitivity. Reject supplier/local-purchase models for missing payments and geography; energy use/cost because solar and PUE are not load; actual abatement, net fiscal benefit, and public cost because bills, executed schedules, distributions, and same-scope costs are absent; and county outcomes for missing causal design. Wider Oxford/Deloitte effects remain context, not re-labeled observations.

source.title: Economic impact of Google data centers in Georgia
source.notes: The study reports Douglas County water consumption for 2022 and 2023, Google's 78.8 MW contracted share of two Georgia solar projects, a 2023 $40,000 Elevate Douglas contribution, and more than $330,000 invested in the Douglas County School System since 2019. project_description: Google operates the Douglas County data-center campus at 300 Riverside Parkway SW in Lithia Springs on a Development Authority of Douglas County tax-abatement parcel. Google dates its local presence to 2003 and its first data-center opening to 2007; the assessor lists data-center improvements with actual years 2006 and 2016 and a utility building from 2011. Public records also document a 2015 expansion, recycled-water cooling, later interior-remodel work, and off-site solar procurement supporting the campus.
